title: Platform systems & services playbook: runbooks, dashboards, alerts, how-tos, roadmap, and retro (Q3 update)
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This page is the canonical platform systems & services playbook for the Platform team. It consolidates: systems and services ownership, common how-tos, dashboard and alert standards, operational runbooks for high-severity incidents, post-incident retrospective template, and the near-term roadmap. Use this page as the first stop for onboarding, incident response, and planning.

Contents
1. Purpose and scope
2. Systems & services inventory and ownership
3. How-tos (common operational procedures)
4. Dashboards and alerting standards
5. Priority runbooks (P0/P1)
6. Retrospective and postmortem template
7. Roadmap and near-term initiatives
8. Contact & escalation matrix
9. Links and references

1) Purpose and scope
- Goal: provide a single, searchable reference for platform engineers and on-call responders that reduces time-to-recovery, enforces consistent observability, and documents planned investments.
- Scope: applies to Platform-managed services and shared infrastructure (monitoring, service mesh, ingress, core data plane, shared caches, internal APIs). Not covered: third-party SaaS vendor runbooks (those live with customer-success or vendor owners).

2) Systems & services inventory and ownership
Short inventory table (core services)
| Service | Owner (Team) | Primary SLA | Notes |
|--------|--------------|-------------|-------|
| platform-api (internal control plane) | platform-backend | 99.95% availability | Critical for deployments and config propagation |
| infra-proxy (ingress / API gateway) | platform-networking | latency p50 < 30ms | Handles multi-tenant routing and rate-limiting |
| kv-cache (shared prefix cache) | runtime-team | p99 latency < 5ms | Used for KV/prefix caching across runtimes |
| telemetry-collector (metrics / traces) | platform-observability | data retention 90d | Ingest for Grafana/Tempo/Prometheus |
| model-routing (smart router) | serving-runtime | p95 routing decision < 15ms | Fallbacks to compatible model variants |

Ownership conventions
- Owner: team responsible for code, capacity, and runbook maintenance. Listed owner is primary pager.
- Backup: secondary team or engineer listed in each service dashboard.

3) How-tos (common operational procedures)
A concise set of standard operating procedures. Each procedure below is a step-by-step checklist.

3.1 Deploy a config change (platform-api)
1. Open the change in GitHub at the repo: github.com/redwood/platform-api (link in team wiki).
2. Ensure unit/integration tests pass and the change is annotated with rollout guidance.
3. Create a canary release: deploy to canary namespace using the pipeline - ci/cd -> deploy-canary.
4. Monitor the canary dashboard for 15 minutes for increased errors, latency, or abnormal traces.
5. If stable, promote to staging, run smoke-tests, then promote to prod with 10% -> 50% -> 100% rollout windows.
6. If errors are observed, rollback using the pipeline rollback step and open an incident if P1.

3.2 Add a dashboard panel (observability)
1. Create a new panel in Grafana with a clear title and description.
2. Use existing metrics naming conventions: service.<service>.metric.<name>.
3. Add thresholds that reflect typical baseline and SLO boundaries.
4. Add drill-down links to logs and traces.
5. Request reviewer from platform-observability for consistency.

3.3 Onboard a new service to platform monitoring
1. Add service to service-catalog.yml and assign owner.
2. Ensure metrics (error_count, request_latency_seconds, success_rate) are emitted.
3. Add logs to centralized ingestion and traces via OpenTelemetry.
4. Create dashboard and baseline for 72h.
5. Create alert rules scoped to service-specific thresholds (see section 4).

4) Dashboards and alerting standards
Principles
- Alert actionable signals only: every alert must map to a runbook page and an owner.
- Use SLO-based alerts for client-facing services; use symptom-based alerts for infra.
- Group metrics by priority: errors -> latency -> saturation -> backlog.

Standard dashboard layout
- Top row: SLO summary (error budget burn, success rate)
- Second row: Key traffic and latency metrics (p50/p95/p99)
- Third row: Errors and top error types (logs sampling links)
- Fourth row: Resource metrics (CPU, GPU, memory, queue depth)
- Bottom row: Dependency health and downstream latencies

Alerting conventions (examples)
| Alert name | Severity | Trigger | Pager | Runbook |
|------------|----------|---------|-------|---------|
| svc.errors.high | P1 | error_count > 50/min AND error_rate > 5% for 2m | owner | /runbooks/svc-errors-high |
| svc.latency.degradation | P2 | p95_latency > 2x baseline for 5m | oncall | /runbooks/svc-latency-degradation |
| infra.ingress.error-spike | P1 | 5xx_rate > 1% for 1m across proxy | platform-networking | /runbooks/ingress-error-spike |
| telemetry.ingest.drop | P1 | metrics_ingest_rate drops > 30% for 2m | platform-observability | /runbooks/telemetry-ingest-drop |

Escalation windows and noise control
- P1: immediate page, 0-15m response expectation. If no ack in 5m escalate to secondary on-call.
- P2: page with 30m response expectation.
- Silence policy: use incident-driven silences for noisy alerts; silences must include owner and justification.

5) Priority runbooks (P0/P1)
We publish runbooks for all P1/P0 scenarios. Each runbook contains: summary, impact, detection, mitigation, rollback steps, stakeholders, post-incident tasks. Examples summarized below.

5.1 Runbook: platform-api outage (P0)
- Summary: platform-api is unavailable and control plane operations failing. Impact: cannot create or update deployments, user-facing model endpoints may degrade.
- Detection: Heartbeat probes failing, > 50% 5xx across the API, deployment controller errors.
- Immediate steps:
  1) Acknowledge pager and declare incident via /incidents/create.
  2) Triage: check recent deploys (Pipeline UI) and config changes.
  3) If a recent config deploy is suspected, rollback to last known-good.
  4) If not deployment-related, gather logs from platform-api pods, check database connectivity, and circuit-breakers.
  5) Activate traffic-reduction policy: throttle non-critical background jobs and pause autoscale actions.
- Mitigation checklist:
  - rollback config -> verify canary status
  - increase replicas if CPU is saturated (see capacity thresholds)
  - apply emergency rate-limit to noisy tenants
- Communication: update status page, send interim update every 15 minutes until resolved.
- Post-incident: run retrospective (section 6), update runbook with any new play.

5.2 Runbook: telemetry ingestion outage (P1)
- Summary: metrics/traces logs ingestion is degraded or delayed. Impact: reduced visibility but services continue to run.
- Immediate steps:
  1) Acknowledge pager and open telemetry incident.
  2) Check retention queue / message backlog length and broker health (kafka/redis).
  3) If backlog growing, scale telemetry-ingesters horizontally.
  4) If downstream store (thanos, tempo) is unhealthy, fail over to read-only nodes and notify infra.
- Recovery: validate ingestion rate returns to baseline and backfill if necessary.

5.3 Runbook: infra-proxy 5xx spike (P1)
- Summary: ingress returning 5xx across multiple tenants.
- Immediate steps:
  1) Check recent deploys to infra-proxy and edge-config.
  2) Collect top 20 traces and error types, identify if a single backend is causing failures.
  3) Apply emergency circuit-breaker for affected backend via admin API.
  4) If load-related, enable temporary rate-limits per tenant and scale proxy pool.
- Communication: add annotated notes to incident timeline and notify affected product teams.

6) Retrospective and postmortem template
Use this template for all P1/P0 incidents. Keep the write-up concise and action-oriented.
- Title: [Service] - Short description - YYYY-MM-DD
- Summary (one paragraph)
- Impact (systems, customers, duration)
- Timeline (concise bullet timeline with timestamps)
- Root cause (one sentence)
- Contributing factors (3-5 bullets)
- Mitigations taken (what fixed it)
- Action items (owner, ETA, verification steps)
- Learnings and follow-ups (links to code/PRs and dashboards)
- Severity review: was alerting appropriate? false-positive? noise?

Retrospective cadence
- P0: full incident review within 7 business days, action items added to roadmap or tracked until closed.
- P1: summary and action items within 14 business days.

7) Roadmap and near-term initiatives (Q2-Q3 2026 focus)
High-level initiatives (owner / target)
- Observability hardening (platform-observability) - goal: reduce alert noise by 40% and achieve 95% linkability of alerts to runbooks by end of Q2.
- Deployment safety automation (platform-backend) - add automated canary promotion based on statistical checks (target: Q2 alpha).
- Smart routing capacity fallback (serving-runtime) - implement region-aware fallback and cost-tier routing (target: Q2 beta).
- Shared cache autoscaling (runtime-team) - autoscale kv-cache based on prefix hotness (target: Q2).
- Playbook modernization (platform) - convert top 10 incident runbooks to step-by-step templates with CLI helpers and webhook integrations (target: Q3).

Prioritization & criteria
- Prioritize items that reduce mean time to recovery (MTTR) or materially reduce unit cost without increasing risk.
- Action items from retrospectives that have customer-impact or recurring incidents get >50% priority weight.

8) Contact & escalation matrix
- Primary on-call: team owner listed in service dashboard.
- Secondary: team backup.
- Platform-wide escalation: if an incident is cross-team or elevated, page Platform EM oncall (pager ID: platform-em-oncall) and CTO incident channel.
- Communications: status.redwood.com is updated by the comms lead; product and sales notifs are handled by CX.

9) Links and references
- Team wiki: /confluence/eng-platform/platform-team-wiki-runbooks-dashboards-roadmap-2026-q1
- Dashboards: Grafana - Platform Overview (link in team wiki)
- On-call rota: /confluence/eng-platform/oncall-schedule
- Incident tooling: /tools/incidents and /tools/playbooks

Appendix A - Sample alert thresholds (recommended defaults)
| Metric | Warning | Critical | Notes |
|--------|---------|----------|-------|
| p95_latency | > 1.5x baseline for 5m | > 2x baseline for 2m | Baseline = 30d rolling median |
| error_rate | > 1% for 2m | > 5% for 1m | For high-throughput services tune by volume |
| cpu_util | > 70% for 10m | > 90% for 5m | Consider horizontal scaling |
| queue_depth | > 50% of capacity | > 90% of capacity | Trigger backpressure or autoscale |

Appendix B - Runbook maintenance checklist
- Review runbooks quarterly during retro sprint.
- Add a one-line change log to each runbook with last_edit and owner.
- Ensure all alerts have a runbook link and owner field.

Document governance
- Owner: eng-platform team (primary), platform-observability (dashboard/alerting standards).
- Review cadence: quarterly or after any P0 incident.
- Edit policy: changes must include reviewer from platform-observability and at least one sign-off from the owning team.

If you have feedback or find missing procedures, add a suggested edit to the page and tag the author and platform-observability.
